format.check: check(policy, amount, payee, now, spentInWindow, escalated) -> expect ('ok' or a §3 reason code)
format.within: within(child, parent) -> expect ('ok' or a §4.1 reason code)
format.window: one account, windowSecs; ops in order: {t, record} adds a spend at t; {t, expect} asserts spentInWindow(t) exactly (§6.1); {t, setWindow} changes windowSecs. An approximate implementation (§6.2) asserts got >= expect and got <= sum of records with t' > t - windowSecs - B for its documented B; vectors marked exactOnly change windowSecs and are for exact implementations only
format.tree: accounts with parent links and policies (every account funded amply); ops in order at time t: spend {from, payee, amount, escalated?} -> expect ok or the first failing reason code walking from the account to the root; fund {from, to, amount} (from MUST be to's parent) and recall {from, of, amount} are internal moves; setPolicy {by, of, policy} where by is an account name (an ancestor's signer) or "owner" -> ok or a §4.1 code; spentInWindow {of} -> expect the exact §6.1 figure
format.x402-exact: check_exact(payment, requirements, chain, spentInWindow, now, escalated, expectedPayer?) -> expect ok (with the extracted spend) or a §7.2 / §3 reason code; chain is the paying account's policy first, then each ancestor; spentInWindow has one figure per policy
format.policy: a policy document -> expect ok or policy_invalid (§2); a binary encoding that cannot represent a value rejects at decode time, which counts as policy_invalid
format.id: a policy document -> its §2.2 id (hex SHA-256 of the canonical wire encoding); implementations that hash a binary struct instead skip this kind and say so
format.meter-check: check(policy, amount, payee, now, spentInWindow, escalated, meter, meterSpentInWindow) -> expect ('ok' or a §3 reason code). As `check`, for policies carrying §2.3 `meters`; `meterDecimals` is what the evaluator determines an asset meter's decimals to be, and is absent when it cannot determine them or when the meter is a unit (nothing external to check against).
format.meter-within: within(child, parent) -> expect ('ok' or a §4.1 code), for policies carrying §2.3 `meters`.
format.meter-policy: a policy document carrying §2.3 `meters` -> expect ok or policy_invalid. Separate from `policy` because §2.3.1's registry rule is semantic, not schema-level: an unregistered unit name is schema-valid and MUST still be rejected at load, so an implementation without §2.3 cannot run these.
